st.t: Assisted inequality: Productivity gains need not improve careers
st.an: The supplied excerpt is only a bibliography. Although it cites research on productivity, legal education, hiring and automation, it provides no attributable findings or argument showing whether the GPT-4 Technical Report accepts the cluster’s proposition that assisted productivity gains need not improve careers or reduce inequality.

st.t: Benchmark governance: High scores may lack workplace meaning
st.an: The supplied GPT-4 Technical Report material contains only bibliographic references and incomplete citation fragments, with no substantive claims, findings or reasoning from which to assess its position on benchmark quality, governance or workplace relevance.

st.t: Professional evaluation: Realistic tasks complicate reproducible scoring
st.an: The supplied GPT-4 Technical Report excerpts are bibliography-only and contain no substantive findings, reasoning, or recommendations. They therefore do not establish whether the source accepts, extends, redirects, or rejects the cluster’s proposition that credible professional AI evaluation must assess realistic task execution while separately validating scoring, automated judging, and self-correction.

st.t: Legal workflows: Immediate gains create competence risks
st.an: The report aligns with the cluster’s core view that current evidence chiefly supports worker augmentation and workflow adaptation, while treating legal-job automation and displacement as future possibilities rather than demonstrated outcomes. It is less specific about bounded legal tasks, verification and competence risks, but does not conflict with them.
qs: However, even using AI as a productivity multiplier requires workers to adjust to new workflows and augment their skills.

st.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment
st.an: The report aligns with the cluster’s core claim that strong task and benchmark performance does not amount to general professional competence. It emphasizes persistent reliability limits, application-specific human review, grounding and context-sensitive deployment, while also noting that productive use requires changed workflows and skills.
qs: While less capable than                                                  humans in many real-world scenarios, GPT-4 exhibits human-level performance                                                  on various professional and academic benchmarks, including passing a simulated                                                  bar exam with a score around the top 10% of test takers.

Great care should be taken when using language model outputs, particularly in high-stakes contexts, with the exact protocol (such as human review, grounding with additional context, or avoiding high-stakes uses altogether) matching the needs of specific applications.
